origins.section: The Interface Belongs to the Policy, So the Policy Compiles Without the Mail Code
A Constructor Parameter Turns a Forgotten Dependency Into a Compile Error
A Fake Checks the Outcome; a Mock Checks the Calls
ServiceLoader Picks the Implementation From the Class Path

recorded.prompt:q-dto-in-their-jar:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-dto-in-their-jar:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-dto-in-their-jar:a: After moving RefundNotifier into billing, '$ javac -Xmaxerrs 1 -d ../out/policy billing/*.java' succeeds with no output while the implementation smtp.SmtpNotifier is in the other jar: 'Now billing compiles alone'. An implementing class is not needed; the missing declaration is what fails.
recorded.prompt:q-dto-in-their-jar:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-dto-in-their-jar:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-dto-in-their-jar:c: billing has no class implementing MailTransport, yet compiling it alone fails: 'billing/RefundPolicy.java:3: error: package smtp does not exist'.
recorded.prompt:q-dto-in-their-jar:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-dto-in-their-jar:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-dto-in-their-jar:d: The compile fails ('package smtp does not exist'), and the error is reported at line 3, 'import smtp.MailTransport;', the naming of the interface type, not at a new expression. The page's code does contain 'new MailTransport.Envelope(...)', but the reported error is the import, so the page shows that naming the type alone requires the jar.
recorded.prompt:q-rate-table-registration:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-rate-table-registration:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-rate-table-registration:a: The locator RefundPolicy has no constructor doing a lookup; Services.get is in refund()'s body, and the output prints 'started' before the failure, which occurs 'at RefundPolicy.refund'.
recorded.prompt:q-rate-table-registration:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-rate-table-registration:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-rate-table-registration:b: The output shows 'started' and 'day 45: false' after the registration line was lost; start-up checks nothing, and the failure comes 'at Services.get' at 'the first approved refund'.
recorded.prompt:q-rate-table-registration:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-rate-table-registration:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-rate-table-registration:d: Outcome right, reason wrong, and the page refutes the reason: a service locator is 'a global map from type to implementation, filled in at start-up'; the failure is from Services.get at call time ('at Services.get(Services.java:14)'), not deferred filling.

recorded.prompt:q-tax-jar-without-services:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tax-jar-without-services:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-tax-jar-without-services:d: Outcome right, reason wrong, and the page refutes the reason: ServiceLoader 'reads ... a file META-INF/services/<interface name> that lists implementation classes'; mail.jar holds both META-INF/MANIFEST.MF and META-INF/services/billing.RefundNotifier, and 'Without the file the class is never found'. The provider names come from the services file, not the manifest.
